newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money eased to 11.0 percent on Wednesday from 12.0/13.0 percent amid a neutral central bank money policy, dealers said.
They said liquidity supply was sufficient, leading one-week and one-month money to soften to 11.25 and 12.5 percent respectively.
One local bank dealer said operators appeared to be calm despite the approaching month-end.
"They think liquidity supply would remain steady because the market was flush even with the new reserve rate. Why should the market be tight next week when we have nothing scheduled."
Dealers said the focus would remain on liquidity but investors were also looking at the start of the election campaign on Sunday.
The central bank offered seven-day bilateral papers (SBIs) at six percent, eight-11 day at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 12.49 percent, compared with 12.9 percent on Monday.
One bond dealer said buying interest was steady despite the upcoming election campaign, with further increases in prices of Astra International bonds.
He said other prices were little changed.
